Subject: Post-call recap: Encryption, residency, retention (next steps)

Hi Carlos / Amanda, 

Thanks for taking the time today. Quick recap from our discovery call and proposed next steps so we're all aligned.

Key items we captured:
- Data scope: PayWise will be sending transaction-level data that includes limited PII (names, emails, last 4 digits of card).
- Residency: EU data residency required for inference and logs for EU customers.
- Retention: Operational logs retention target = 90 days; PII retention for derived assets = 30 days (customer-managed).
- Logging & audit: Need redaction of PII in logs by default, with audit log export (read-only) for compliance.
- Encryption requirements: TLS 1.2+ in-transit; at-rest encryption with customer-managed keys (CMK) preferred; support for AWS KMS, Azure Key Vault, and HSM/BYOK required.

What we will send today (attached):
- Redwood SOC 2 summary (redwood-soc2-summary.pdf)
- KMS & CMK options overview (kms-options-overview.pdf)

Suggested next steps:
1) Technical deep-dive with our SE (30-45m) to review BYOK flow, key import/rotation, and EU-region deployment - propose Wed 2026-07-14 10:00 CET / 01:00 PT.
2) Sean to provide short architecture note (how KMS integrates, TLS config, redaction hooks).
3) You to confirm any additional registry/vendor constraints (e.g., must use Azure Key Vault with HSM).

Carlos, can you confirm the proposed time and whether you want us to bring a short diagram showing where keys live and what we store? Also, please send the most recent security questionnaire if you want us to pre-populate answers (we got a nod that you'd share one).

Thanks,
Marissa

- PII: We must ensure PII is not present in logs by default. If retention of PII is required for debugging, it needs to be opt-in per environment and logged.

From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Carlos Vega <carlos.vega@paywise.com>

Subject: Re: Post-call recap: Encryption, residency, retention (next steps) - SE details

Hi all, thanks, Marissa / Carlos. Quick technical responses and what I'll bring to the deep-dive: 

Summary answers:
- In-transit: TLS 1.2+ enforced (we support TLS1.3). Mutual TLS for service-to-service connections is supported for enterprise Private deployments.
- At-rest: We encrypt all data at-rest with AES-256. For customer-managed keys (CMK) we integrate with: AWS KMS, Azure Key Vault (including HSM-backed keys), and GCP KMS.
- BYOK: We support BYOK via key references to customer-managed KMS (no key material is stored by Redwood). For Azure Key Vault we support both using existing key identities and Customer-Managed Keys (CMKs) with an RBAC-based access model. Key import into an Azure HSM is handled on the customer side - Redwood references the key via its Key Identifier.
- Key rotation: Rotation is supported. We can either accept a rotated key ID pushed by the customer or poll the KMS per your rotation schedule. Automated rotation with zero-downtime requires coordination; we'll outline the recommended rotation workflow in the note.
- Regional restrictions: We can restrict key usage per deployment/region by scoping the instance to the EU region and pointing to your EU KMS endpoint.
- Logs & Audit: We can export audit logs to your Azure Blob or S3 daily. Operational logs used for debugging are redacted by default (PII fields masked). If you enable extended debugging, PII capture is opt-in and writes to a customer-controlled, short-lived bucket.

I'll prepare:
- 1-page architecture diagram (where keys live, what Redwood stores, typical request flow)
- Key rotation workflow doc (90-day rotation example, steps for Azure KV + HSM)
- Example IAM policy snippets for giving Redwood read/use access to a key without key export rights
- Pre-filled answers for the security questionnaire sections on encryption and logging

Proposed deep-dive agenda (30-45m):
1) Architecture overview (10m)
2) KMS integration flow & BYOK (10m)
3) Log redaction & audit export (10m)
4) Q&A / next steps (10-15m)

I can join at Wed 2026-07-14 10:00 CET. See calendar invite link: https://calendar.redwood.com/meet/tech-deep-dive-20260714
